definition: In machine learning, embedding is a representation learning technique that maps complex, high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional vector space of numerical vectors..
details: In machine learning, embedding is a representation learning technique that maps complex, high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional vector space of numerical vectors.

explainer.lead: An embedding turns complicated, high-dimensional data into a shorter list of numbers that a model can work with. This learned, compact representation makes the data easier to process while reducing its dimensionality.

tiers.eli5: Imagine describing a huge, detailed object with just a few numbers, like giving its location on a small map. An embedding learns how to make that shorter description. It does not keep the original data unchanged; it gives it a more compact numerical form.
tiers.practitioner: Use an embedding as a learned mapping from high-dimensional features to a lower-dimensional vector, then pass that vector to another part of a machine-learning system. The output dimension is a design choice, and reducing it means the vector cannot simply be treated as a copy of the original input. Avoid interpreting individual coordinates as meaningful unless that interpretation has been established separately.
tiers.paperLevel: An embedding can be written as f: X -> R^d, where X contains complex, high-dimensional data and f is learned through representation learning. For an input x, f(x) is a numerical vector in a space with fewer dimensions than the original representation. The definition alone does not specify the learning objective or which properties of x are preserved.

explainer.example: Suppose an input is represented by 10,000 numbers. An embedding could map that representation to the three-dimensional vector [0.8, -0.2, 1.1], replacing 10,000 coordinates with three.
explainer.intuition: An embedding is like translating a detailed description into a short set of coordinates. The goal is a learned numerical representation that is smaller and easier for a model to handle.
howItWorks: Start with complex data represented in a high-dimensional space.
Learn a mapping that processes that representation.
Apply the mapping to produce a numerical vector.
Use the resulting lower-dimensional vector as the data's embedded representation.
explainer.whyItMatters: Embeddings give machine-learning models a compact numerical form for complex data. They connect representation learning with downstream processing in a lower-dimensional vector space.
misconceptions: An embedding is not the original data; it is a transformed representation.
Lower-dimensional does not mean the representation is lossless.
Individual vector coordinates are not automatically human-interpretable.

diagram.caption: An embedding learns to map a high-dimensional representation into a compact numerical vector.
